{"id": "d0da1ac9-7176-49e7-b372-4664e41844c8", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_iWrirJMTfvE92z4Q7Wx71L", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"How do I optimize the performance of my Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes?\",\"context\":\"### Match workload demand to provisioned IOPS\\n\\nTake the following actions:\\n\\n* Confirm that your workload demand doesn't exceed the IOPS that you provision.\\n* If I/O latency is high, then check the average queue length to confirm your application isn't driving more IOPS than provisioned.\\n* If IOPS demand exceeds your provisioned amount and the application is latency sensitive, then increase the Provisioned IOPS on your volume.\\n\\nFor more information, see [Amazon EBS-optimized instance types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-ec2-config.html) and [Amazon EBS I/O characteristics and monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-io-characteristics.html)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/optimize-ebs-provisioned-iops\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How do I choose the right Amazon EBS volume type for my workload?\",\"context\":\"### Compare provisioned IOPS SSD volumes\\n\\n[Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html) include **io2** Block Express volumes and **io1** volumes. If you require more durability and a higher IOPS-to-GiB ratio, then use **io2** Block Express.\\n\\n**Note:** All **io2** volumes created after November 21, 2023, are **io2** Block Express volumes. To convert **io2** volumes created before November 21, 2023, to **io2** Block Express volumes, [modify the IOPS or size of the volume](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html).\\n\\n**Important:** If you created your **io1** volume before December 6, 2017, then you must upgrade the volume to io2 Block Express. Make sure that you provisioned 64,000 IOPS to reach the maximum 1,000 MB/s throughput.\\n\\nThe maximum values for IOPS, throughput, and latency are based on an I/O size of 16 KiB. A larger I/O size can't reach these maximum values.\\n\\nUse the following specifications to determine whether **io1** or **io2** Block Express meets your performance and durability requirements:\\n\\n| Specification | io1 | io2 Block Express |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| **Volume size** | 4 GB \u2013 16 TB | 4 GB \u2013 64 TB |\\n| **Max IOPS/volume** | 64,000 | 256,000 |\\n| **Max throughput/volume** | 1,000 MB/s | 4,000 MB/s |\\n| **Max IOPS/GB** | 50 IOPS/GB | 1,000 IOPS/GB |\\n| **Durability** | 99.8% \u2013 99.9% | 99.999% |\\n| **Multi-Attach support** | Supported | Supported |\\n| **Boot volume** | Supported | Supported |\\n| **Latency** | Single-digit millisecond | Sub-millisecond (average under 500 microseconds for 16 KiB I/O) |\\n| **Instance availability** | All EC2 instances | All EC2 instances built on the [AWS Nitro System](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/nitro/) |\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-volume-type-differences\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Class: Aws::EC2::Types::ScheduledInstancesEbs\\n \\n \u2014 AWS SDK for Ruby V2\",\"context\":\"### #**iops** \u21d2 Integer\\n\\nThe number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for an `io1`\\nor `io2` volume, with a maximum ratio of 50 IOPS/GiB for `io1`, and 500\\nIOPS/GiB for `io2`. Range is 100 to 64,000 IOPS for volumes in most\\nRegions. Maximum IOPS of 64,000 is guaranteed only on Nitro-based\\ninstances. Other instance families guarantee performance up to\\n32,000 IOPS. For more information, see Amazon EBS Volume Types in\\nthe *Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide*.\\n\\nThis parameter is valid only for Provisioned IOPS SSD (`io1` and `io2`)\\nvolumes.\\n\\nReturns:\\n\\n* (Integer)\\n \u2014\\n\\n The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for an `io1` or `io2` volume, with a maximum ratio of 50 IOPS/GiB for `io1`, and 500 IOPS/GiB for `io2`\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-ruby/v2/api/Aws/EC2/Types/ScheduledInstancesEbs.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up EBS io2 IOPS quota documentation"}

{"id": "b30ae9ac-c939-42c3-a175-bd9cab3faddb", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Your quota is too low for this volume. The io2 IOPS quota is a **Region-wide total across all your io2 volumes**, not a per-volume cap. I checked your account in us-east-1, and it shows:

| Quota | Current value | Adjustable |
|---|---|---|
| IOPS for Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes (`L-8D977E7E`) | 100,000 | Yes |
| Storage for io2 volumes (`L-09BD8365`) | 20 TiB | Yes |
| Storage modifications for io2 volumes (`L-9A0E0F82`) | 20 TiB | Yes |

**What to do**

1. **Request a quota increase.** Raise `L-8D977E7E` in Service Quotas.
   - Existing io2 volumes in the Region count toward the total. The new quota needs to cover your current provisioned IOPS plus the 150K you want to add.
   - If you already have 50K IOPS provisioned, you need at least 200K.
   - Request a bit of headroom above that.
   - Increases for this quota can take some time to approve, so submit the request early.
2. **Check the storage quota too.** The 20 TiB limit applies to total io2 capacity in the Region. This matters if you're also adding a lot of capacity.
3. **Check that the volume itself is valid.** These are the per-volume limits for io2 Block Express, based on the docs:
   - It supports up to 256,000 IOPS per volume. Your 150K is within that.
   - The ratio is at most 1,000 IOPS per GiB, so you need at least a 150 GiB volume for 150K IOPS.
   - Reaching these IOPS needs a Nitro-based instance. Your instance type must also support that much EBS IOPS, because many instances cap out lower.

**Workarounds if you can't wait**
- Free up quota by lowering the IOPS on, or removing, other io2 volumes in the Region.
- Create the volume in a different Region where you have unused quota.
- Provision less than 150K IOPS for now, up to what's left under your quota. You can raise it later with a volume modification once the increase is approved.

I can submit the quota increase request for you. It would need your approval before it runs. Tell me the new IOPS value you want, or tell me to work it out from your existing io2 volumes. I can also total your current io2 IOPS first.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
